top_choice_rationale: P001 awards the optical lattice clock to Katori and Ye. The magic-wavelength condition removes Doppler and recoil shifts and lets many atoms be interrogated at once. The systematics are understood term by term, and independent clocks at JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, NIST and SYRTE agree at the 10^-18 level. The invention is mature, reproducible across laboratories and has already opened new regimes (gravitational redshift over millimetres, limits on drifting constants, dark-matter searches). The two-name allocation and the citation scope are defensible, and all eight members explicitly support this configuration. No award would withhold a well-founded prize for no scientific reason.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile for the optical lattice clock; as WACQT director and a superconducting-circuits theorist I have no direct link to Katori or Ye
